accessibility.description: Grafik titik-titik biru untuk suku barisan a_n=n/(1+n) terhadap indeks n. Titik-titik meningkat dari bawah dan mendekati garis horizontal pada tinggi 1. Dua garis horizontal ungu pada tinggi 1-\epsilon dan 1+\epsilon membatasi pita; setelah suatu indeks, semua titik barisan berada di dalam pita tersebut.

source_corrections.evidence: the epsilon definition and chosen threshold require the non-strict inequality
source_corrections.source_issue: the hypothesis uses n greater than or equal to N but the proof writes the stricter n greater than N
source_corrections.target_action: use n greater than or equal to N consistently

source_corrections.evidence: the surrounding comparison uses arbitrary points x and y
source_corrections.source_issue: the Euclidean-distance equality has d_E(a,y) on the left but absolute value x-y on the right
source_corrections.target_action: replace the first argument a with x

source_corrections.evidence: a point of R squared requires the two coordinates y_1 and y_2
source_corrections.source_issue: the taxicab metric repeats the coordinates y_1,y_1
source_corrections.target_action: replace the second occurrence with y_1,y_2

source_corrections.evidence: the section title and all following results concern sequential characterizations of continuity
source_corrections.source_issue: the phrase different ways to characterize is missing its mathematical object
source_corrections.target_action: state that the section gives different ways to characterize continuity

source_corrections.evidence: the theorem assumes a_n converges to a and asserts continuity of f
source_corrections.source_issue: the proof states that the limit of f(a_n) equals a rather than f(a)

source_corrections.evidence: the repaired phrase is the continuity of f
source_corrections.source_issue: the phrase the f continuity of f contains a stray f

source_corrections.evidence: the sentence describes a proof method
source_corrections.source_issue: be finding is a typographical error
source_corrections.target_action: translate the intended phrase by finding

source_corrections.evidence: the summary statement requires an indefinite article and no variable m
source_corrections.source_issue: to m metric space contains a stray m
source_corrections.target_action: translate the intended phrase to a metric space

source_corrections.evidence: the displayed infimum uses set-builder notation opened earlier in the same expression
source_corrections.source_issue: the point-to-set distance formula is missing its closing set brace

source_corrections.evidence: the exercise concerns a sequence of rational numbers converging in the real numbers
source_corrections.source_issue: the ambient real-number symbol is plain R rather than the established real-number macro

source_corrections.evidence: the standard space C[0,1] and the following supremum metric both use the compact interval domain
source_corrections.source_issue: C[0,1] is described as continuous functions from R to R
source_corrections.target_action: state continuous functions from [0,1] to R

source_corrections.evidence: the same exercise defines and uses C[0,1]

the subspace metric is the restriction of the ambient metric, so convergence to a point of Y is equivalent in the two spaces; the sqrt(2) example instead demonstrates failure of convergence in Y when the ambient limit lies outside Y
source_corrections.source_issue: the rational sequence converging to sqrt(2) is called a counterexample to the literal converse although the retained converse assumes the limit a lies in the subspace Y
source_corrections.target_action: state that the literal converse with all hypotheses retained is true; then present the example only as ambient convergence to a point outside the subspace

source_corrections.evidence: the paragraph and list are consecutive siblings; the cumulative Chapters 1-9 wrapper passes the pinned PreTeXt 1.7.5 RelaxNG validation
source_corrections.source_issue: the unordered list is nested inside a paragraph element and violates the pinned PreTeXt content model
source_corrections.target_action: close the introductory paragraph before the unordered list while preserving element order and prose

source_corrections.evidence: the sequence is (f_n), while its proposed pointwise limit is the single function f defined immediately above
source_corrections.source_issue: the target function f is written as the parenthesized expression (f), which incorrectly resembles a one-term sequence
source_corrections.target_action: write the convergence target as the function f
